The time had passed too quickly.
Just like in the beginning.
I raised my fist in the air before I left the podium.
entradas.menu: Raise your fist.

entradas.text: I waved at the crowd before I left the podium.
entradas.menu: Wave.

entradas.text: I raised my hand and formed a victory sign before I left the podium.
entradas.menu: Make a victory sign.

entradas.text: That was it. The elections were approaching once again.
"I promise you. We will remind everyone that the Republic of Sordland is the grea–"
entradas.menu: "I promise you. We will remind everyone that the Republic of Sordland is the greatest nation in the world."

entradas.text: "We are still all fired up. We are still ready to go. Let us fin–"
entradas.menu: "We are still all fired up. We are still ready to go. Let us finish what we started!"

entradas.text: "We will keep building our dream of Sord–"
entradas.menu: "We have been building our dream of Sordland -- the great Sordish Dream -- and today, in this square, that dream is renewed."

entradas.text: Suddenly, I felt a sharp pain in my abdomen.
"Thank you, Mr. Rayne."
"I believe our movement will give birth to an honorable future. Today, the future belongs to the Sords. To Sordland."
"I don't want to use the words that every USP politician repeats. But it is true that the morning is finally coming..."
"This time, however, victory is not theirs. It's ours. It's everybody's."
"So for the final time... Sordland! A Morgna wes core!"
Thunderous applause erupted. Everyone responded, "Vectern sis da!"
"Thank you, Mr. Rayne."
"I believe our movement will give birth to an honorable future. Today, the future belongs to the Sords. To Sordland."
Thunderous applause erupted. Everyone yelled, "Sordland!"
"Greci Sordland!"

It was the biggest gathering of people we'd managed to assemble during my campaign, and if my advisors were right, it was also the largest ever assembled in the Maroon Square -- used to be known as Soll Square.
Karl's approach interrupted my thoughts. He saluted.
"We secured the entire area and we are ready for any possibility, sir."
"I assigned my best men to join the crowd in disguise."
"Thank you, Karl. Good work."
entradas.menu: "Thank you, Karl. Good work."

entradas.text: "This better not be another inauguration ball."
entradas.menu: "This better not be another inauguration ball."

entradas.text: "Isn't that a little too much?"
entradas.menu: "Isn't that a little too much?"

entradas.text: "We all know what is at stake, sir."
"It will not be, sir."
"Thank you, sir."
"I will be close by just in case."
"Good luck with your speech, sir."
He saluted again and left me alone.
Around me, I saw a sea of Maroon Party banners and flags. It was as if people had painted the square red.
I paced back and forth behind the stage, gathering my strength. This was the last major event before the election. A massive crowd awaited me.
